The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

This Appeal is filed by the Insurance Company aggrieved by the judgment and award passed in M.V.C. No.501/2014 by the III Additional Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Kalaburagi, dated 28.09.2017 questioning the NC: 2024:KHC-K:1564 liability and the quantum of compensation and also claiming that there is contributory negligence.

entities.text: III Additional Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Kalaburagi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The claim petition was filed seeking compensation, on account of the injuries suffered by the claimant in the road traffic accident.

It is the case of the claimant that on 04.02.2014 at about 7:30 p.m., he along with another person was proceeding on Motorcycle, at that time the Driver of Auto Rickshaw came in opposite side with high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed the motorcycle of the claimant, due to which, he fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately he was shifted to the Government Hospital, Gulbarga, wherein, he took treatment as inpatient from 04.02.2014 to 25.02.1014 and spent huge amount towards treatment.

According to him he was earning Rs.9,000/- per month by working as a Mason and the Doctor has opined that he had sustained 18% disability to the whole body and the Tribunal considering the disability at 10% to the whole body granted the compensation as per the table given NC: 2024:KHC-K:1564 below and held that the Insurance Company is liable to pay the compensation:

Learned counsel appearing for the Insurance Company submits that the Driver of the Auto Rickshaw was not having valid and effective Driving License as on the date of accident as it is a commercial transport vehicle and he was holding License to drive a light motor vehicle.
It is submitted that though there is material to show that he is not having valid Driving License, the Tribunal NC: 2024:KHC-K:1564 fastened the liability on the Insurance Company.

It is further submitted that the accident had taken place in the middle of the road which itself shows contributory negligence on the part of the claimant and this aspect was not considered by the Tribunal.

Coming to the quantum of compensation it is submitted that as per the Doctor the fracture sustained by the claimant is healed and the Tribunal without any basis had taken 10% disability to the whole body.
It is also submitted that the amount awarded is on the higher side.
4. Learned counsel appearing for the respondent No.1-claimant submits that in fact the compensation that was awarded by the Tribunal is on the lower side.
Without there being any appeal, this Court can consider the case of the claimant for enhancement of the compensation.

It is submitted that in the light of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Mukund Dewangan vs. NC: 2024:KHC-K:1564 Oriental Ins. Co. Ltd.,1 the Insurance Company is liable to pay the compensation.

entities.text: Mukund Dewangan vs. NC: 2024:KHC-K:1564 Oriental Ins. Co. Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel submits that no grounds are made out by the Insurance Company and it is liable to be dismissed and the claimant is entitled for enhancement of the compensation.
5. Having heard the learned counsels on either side, perused the material on record.

6. In this case the Driver of the Auto Rickshaw was having License to drive a Light Motor Vehicle,
but according to them there is no endorsement.
In the light of the law laid down in Mukund Dewangan's case the said issue is no more res-integra and the Insurance Company is liable to pay the compensation.
7. Coming to the ground of contributory negligence, except relying on the Spot Sketch no evidence is adduced by the Insurance Company.

The burden lies on 2017 SUPREME COURT 3668 NC:
2024:KHC-K:1564 the Insurance Company when they plead that there is contributory negligence.

In The Reliance General Insurance vs Zainuddin And Anr on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30788116/
3 that view of the matter this Court holds that there is no material to show that there is contributory negligence on the part of the claimant.

entities.text: Reliance General Insurance vs Zainuddin And Anr on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 8. Then coming to the quantum of compensation, the Insurance Company is disputing the percentage of disability.
The doctor has stated that claimant had sustained 18% disability, but the Tribunal had taken 10% as disability.
Just because the fracture is healed that itself cannot be a ground for the Insurance Company to submit that there is no disability.
The Doctor's evidence is consistent and he has also stated on what basis he has come to such conclusion.
In that view of the matter, this Court finds no reason to interfere.

Coming to the enhancement of the compensation,
without there being any appeal, this Court cannot consider the case of the claimant for enhancement of the compensation.
Accordingly, the Appeal is dismissed.
i) The amount in deposit and the Trial Court Records shall be forthwith transferred to the Tribunal.
ii) No costs.
Pending I.As., if any, shall stand closed.
